Apple___Apple_scab.about: Fungal disease (Venturia inaequalis) that thrives in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves; scabby, cracked lesions on fruit.
actions: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn
Prune for airflow so leaves dry quickly
Use a protectant fungicide from green tip, following local spray advice
Prefer scab-resistant varieties when replanting

Apple___Black_rot.about: Fungal disease (Botryosphaeria obtusa) that affects leaves, fruit and bark.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-edged brown 'frogeye' leaf spots, rotting fruit with dark rings, cankers on branches.
actions: Prune out cankers and dead wood and burn or bin it
Remove mummified fruit from the tree and ground
Keep trees vigorous and avoid wounding bark
Apply fungicide per local advice if pressure is high

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.about: Fungal disease (Gymnosporangium) that needs both apple and juniper/cedar hosts.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface, later tiny tube-like structures underneath.
actions: Remove nearby juniper or cedar galls where practical
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties
Apply protectant fungicide from pink bud through petal fall, per local advice

Apple___healthy.about: No visible disease symptoms on this leaf.
Apple___healthy.symptoms: Even green colour, no spots, lesions, mould or curling.
actions: Keep monitoring the plant regularly
Water at the base and keep foliage dry
Remove fallen leaves and weeds to limit future disease

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.about: Fungal disease (Podosphaera) favoured by warm days and humid nights.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery growth on leaves, curling or distorted new shoots.
actions: Prune to open the canopy and improve airflow
Avoid excess nitrogen that pushes soft growth
Apply sulfur or another labelled fungicide early, per local advice

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.about: Fungal disease (Cercospora zeae-maydis), worse in humid weather and in maize-after-maize fields.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Narrow rectangular tan to gray lesions running between the leaf veins.
actions: Rotate away from maize for at least a year
Bury or manage crop residue
Choose tolerant hybrids
Fungicide around tasseling only if disease is severe, per local advice

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.about: Fungal disease (Puccinia sorghi) spread by wind-blown spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
actions: Plant resistant hybrids
Scout early; most healthy crops tolerate light infection
Consider fungicide only if pustules are heavy before tasseling

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.about: Fungal disease (Exserohilum turcicum) favoured by moderate temperatures and long leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped gray-green to tan lesions, often 3-15 cm.
actions: Rotate crops and manage residue
Choose resistant hybrids
Fungicide at early tasseling if lesions reach the ear leaf, per local advice

Grape___Black_rot.about: Fungal disease (Guignardia bidwellii) active from budbreak in warm, wet weather.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Tan leaf spots with dark borders and tiny black dots; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
actions: Remove mummified berries and infected canes
Open the canopy for airflow and sun
Apply protectant fungicide from early shoot growth, per local advice

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).about: Trunk-disease complex caused by several wood-rotting fungi; there is no cure.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow and brown bands between leaf veins, dark spotting on berries, sudden vine collapse in summer.
actions: Prune in dry weather and protect pruning wounds
Cut out or remove badly affected vines and burn the wood
Use clean planting material for new vines

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.about: Fungal leaf spot (Pseudocercospora vitis), most common late in the season.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Dark brown angular spots, leaves yellow and fall early.
actions: Rake and remove fallen leaves
Improve airflow in the canopy
Apply labelled fungicide if it recurs, per local advice

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Even green colour, no spots, lesions, mould or curling.
actions: Keep monitoring the plant regularly

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).about: Bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid. It is incurable and serious.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetrical yellow mottling, small lopsided bitter fruit, twig dieback.
actions: Report suspected trees to your agricultural authority
Control psyllids on all citrus nearby
Remove confirmed infected trees as advised locally
Only plant certified disease-free nursery stock

Peach___Bacterial_spot.about: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni), worse in warm, wet, windy weather.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular water-soaked spots that turn purple-brown and drop out ('shot-hole'); pitted fruit spots.
actions: Plant tolerant varieties
Keep trees well fed and not drought-stressed
Apply copper or labelled bactericide during the season, per local advice
Avoid overhead irrigation

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.about: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas) carried on seed and plant debris.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots turning brown with yellow halos; rough raised spots on fruit.
actions: Use clean seed and healthy transplants
Rotate away from peppers and tomatoes for 2-3 years
Avoid overhead watering and handling wet plants
Copper-based sprays can slow spread, per local advice

Potato___Early_blight.about: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani), common on stressed or ageing plants.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark spots with concentric 'target' rings on older leaves, yellowing around them.
actions: Rotate crops and use certified seed
Keep plants well fed and watered to reduce stress
Remove infected debris after harvest
Apply protectant fungicide if it spreads, per local advice

Potato___Late_blight.about: Water mould (Phytophthora infestans); spreads very fast in cool, humid weather and can destroy a crop in days.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked blotches, white fuzzy growth on the underside in humid weather, firm brown tuber rot.
actions: Act immediately: remove and bag infected plants
Apply a labelled fungicide on a protective schedule, per local advice
Avoid overhead watering and destroy volunteer plants and cull piles
Use certified seed tubers

Squash___Powdery_mildew.about: Fungal disease that thrives in warm days, cool nights and dry leaf surfaces.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves that spread and turn leaves brown and brittle.
actions: Space plants for airflow and full sun
Plant resistant varieties
Sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or oil sprays can help early
Remove heavily infected leaves

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.about: Fungal disease (Diplocarpon earlianum), common in wet weather and dense beds.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small purple spots that merge, so leaves look scorched.
actions: Remove old infected leaves after harvest
Do not overcrowd plants; renew beds regularly
Water at the base, not overhead
Plant tolerant cultivars

Strawberry___healthy.about: No visible disease symptoms on this leaf.
Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Even green colour, no spots, lesions, mould or curling.
actions: Keep monitoring the plant regularly
Water at the base and keep foliage dry

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.about: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas) spread by splashing water and wet handling.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark greasy spots with yellow halos on leaves; scabby raised spots on fruit.
actions: Use disease-free seed and transplants
Do not work in wet plants
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops
Copper-based sprays can slow spread, per local advice

Tomato___Early_blight.about: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani), usually starting on lower, older leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric 'target' rings and yellow halos; stem and fruit lesions.
actions: Remove lower infected leaves and debris
Mulch and stake plants to keep leaves off the soil
Rotate crops for 2-3 years
Apply protectant fungicide if it keeps spreading, per local advice

Tomato___Late_blight.about: Water mould (Phytophthora infestans); explosive in cool, humid weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Greasy gray-green to brown patches, white fuzz underneath in humid weather, firm brown fruit rot.
actions: Remove and bag infected plants quickly
Do not compost infected material
Keep foliage dry; water at the base
Apply protectant fungicide before conditions turn wet, per local advice

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.about: Fungal disease (Passalora fulva), typical in greenhouses and humid conditions.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches on the upper leaf, olive-green velvety mould underneath.
actions: Ventilate and lower humidity
Space plants and prune for airflow
Remove infected leaves
Use resistant varieties; fungicide if needed, per local advice

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.about: Fungal disease (Septoria lycopersici), splash-spread from soil and debris.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and gray centres, often with tiny black specks; starts on lower leaves.
actions: Remove infected lower leaves
Mulch to stop soil splash
Avoid overhead watering
Rotate crops for 3 years; fungicide if needed, per local advice

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.about: Tiny sap-sucking pests, not a fungus; explode in hot, dry weather.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling, bronzing leaves, fine webbing on the underside.
actions: Spray plants with a strong jet of water
Insecticidal soap or horticultural oil on leaf undersides
Reduce dust and water-stress; encourage predatory mites
Miticide only if severe, per local advice

Tomato___Target_Spot.about: Fungal disease (Corynespora cassiicola) favoured by warm, humid, dense canopies.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and yellow halos; sunken fruit lesions.
actions: Improve airflow by pruning and staking
Remove infected leaves and debris
Rotate crops
Apply labelled fungicide if needed, per local advice

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.about: Virus spread by whiteflies. There is no cure.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upwards and yellow at the edges, plants stunted, few fruit.
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants early
Control whiteflies (netting, sticky traps, reflective mulch)
Plant tolerant or resistant varieties
Use virus-free transplants

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.about: Highly contagious virus spread by contact, tools and seed. There is no cure.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling, distorted narrow leaves, stunted growth.
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants
Wash hands and disinfect tools between plants
Do not handle tomatoes after tobacco products
Use resistant varieties and clean seed
